analysis_steps.goal: Decompose spectra and measure outflow v_out, flux and R_out

method.value: Multi-Gaussian fit to nuclear/aperture spectra with visual choice of host components; v_out=|dv|+FW10%/2; S_CO(wings) integrates the broad component where it contributes >50%; R_out=|dR|+FWHM/2 from UV-plane Gaussian fit to outflow velocity range

evidence.quote: fit multiple Gaussians to the spectrum which, is the sum of host emission and (if present) broad outflow. Visual inspection is used to choose the number of Gaussians needed to fit the host emission.

claims.hypothesis: High FIR surface brightness galaxies commonly host molecular outflows
claims.experiment: CO(1-0) NOEMA/ALMA search plus literature for the Lutz+16 sample
claims.result: 13 of 17 sources with deep CO data show outflows
claims.finding: High Sigma_FIR galaxies are good hunting grounds for outflows, but not sufficient for all

evidence.quote: 17 of 18 sources in the (cite: lutz16) sample now have suitable CO data, and 13 of these exhibit molecular outflows.

claims.hypothesis: CO-based and OH-based outflow properties are consistent
claims.experiment: Compare combined CO sample with OH P-Cygni results and 12 ULIRG models
claims.result: Masses and velocities agree within ~0.3 and 0.08 dex dispersion; radii differ by ~0.5 dex
claims.finding: Cross-validation of the methods and support for alpha_CO=0.8

evidence.quote: the comparisons provide a very successful cross-validation of the OH P-Cygni and CO interferometric methods of characterizing molecular outflows

claims.hypothesis: CO outflows are optically thin and alpha_CO is low
claims.experiment: Compare CO(1-0) wings with higher-J lines for four sources
claims.result: R_i1<~1 for three; R31=2.1 in IRAS 13120-5453
claims.finding: Mostly optically thick, but alpha_CO may vary between outflows

evidence.quote: The high $R_{31}=2.1$ in IRAS 13120-5453 clearly indicates that this outflow is optically thin in CO.

claims.hypothesis: Outflow driving involves intermittent AGN activity
claims.experiment: Flow times, energy and momentum budgets vs AGN luminosity, fossil outflows
claims.result: Median flow time 1.5 Myr; some outflows in non-AGN hosts exceed AGN budgets; NGC 2623 fossil outflow
claims.finding: Short flow times and multiple episodes support intermittent, likely AGN, driving

evidence.quote: Short $\sim 10^6$ yr flow times and some sources with spatially resolved multiple outflow episodes support a role of intermittent/episodic driving, likely by AGN.

evidence.quote: make it an obvious basis for a search for local outflow laboratories, well suited for detailed study

evidence.quote: we conservatively identify outflowing gas with line wings only
